content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-22 (apparatus claims 1-12, 13-17 and method claims 18-22), every entry in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part and relationship in the Summary and Detailed Description, and all seven figure briefs were checked against the affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and the USER passage in input/conversation.md. Result of the source trace: no untraced technical assertion was found. Each of rail/lower face/upper face/longitudinal slot/printed distance marks; fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, with a downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge; reversibility by two screws in two corresponding holes with the projecting portion moving from one longitudinal side to the opposite side and the same marked face still readable; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate guide carriages with lower keys that block rotation while permitting sliding; one cylindrical drill bushing per carriage with a bore passing completely through and registering with the slot, the two bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob above the rail with a shank through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail that clamps the rail between carriage and shoe; a pointer on each carriage aligned with its bore axis and readable against the distance marks with the reading difference giving center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint and shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with it and sighted on a pencil centerline; the full method sequence (select spacing, loosen, slide to centered readings, tighten, place, press fence or spacer against the edge, align notch and index to the centerline, drill both bushings, lift away with nothing remaining attached); rigid polymer or metal for rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, spacer plate, pointers and knobs, hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network limitation each maps to an exact affirmative disclosure sentence. Prior-art characterizations in the Background were not traced to the inventor, as instructed. Terminology required by the brief (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch) is preserved; no means-plus-function language, no placeholders, drafting notes, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain; numerals are one-to-one with parts and every numeral appears in at least one figure; claim antecedent basis is complete; section lines 3-3 and 5-5 carry the same repeated designation in the FIG. 2 source brief, in the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 resulting-view briefs, and in the Brief Description; and no application text justifies a renderer's shape choice with "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language. Two internal-consistency defects were found in the drawing specifications and are reported: the FIG. 4 brief identifies the workpiece edge 92 as the upper side of the edgewise panel while simultaneously placing the rail's lower face 14 on that same front face and the spacer plate 40 vertically between the downwardly projecting portion 32 and that edge, which cannot both be drawn; and the FIG. 2 (and FIG. 1) briefs show the whole length of the rail including its second end yet omit the transverse center index 24 and the shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 that the description and claims require to be present at the midpoint and in the second end, so the same rail would be depicted with and without those features. Both are drawing-brief wording defects, not source-fidelity gaps, and each has a filing-clean fix given below.

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief identifies the workpiece edge 92 as the upper side of the panel, contradicting the rail resting on the front face and the spacer plate standing against that edge
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph 2 (and paragraphs 3 and 5 of the same brief)
findings.detail: In a side elevation the panel is seen edgewise, so its upper long side is the front face on which the rail's lower face 14 rests, and the workpiece edge 92 is the short end face at the left against which the downwardly projecting portion 32 (or the spacer plate 40) bears. The brief instead calls the upper side of the panel the workpiece edge 92, which cannot be reconciled with the two later statements in the same brief that the rail rests on the front face with its lower face 14 on that front face, and that the spacer plate 40 stands vertically between the downwardly projecting portion 32 and the workpiece edge 92. As written the renderer would place the edge that the fence grips on the same surface the rail lies on. This also conflicts with the description, which recites both a front face and a separate workpiece edge 92 of the workpiece 90.
findings.evidence: FIG-4.md: "The workpiece 90 is seen edgewise as a flat panel, and its straight upper side is the workpiece edge 92." versus, in the same brief, "The rail 10 rests on the front face of the workpiece 90, with its lower face 14 on that front face" and "The spacer plate 40 is a flat plate standing between the downwardly projecting portion 32 and the workpiece edge 92, with one face against the downwardly projecting portion 32 and the opposite face against the workpiece edge 92." Description: "The workpiece 90 is a cabinet door or a drawer front having a front face and at least one straight workpiece edge 92."
findings.fix: Replace the sentence in figures/FIG-4.md with: "The workpiece 90 is seen edgewise as a flat panel, its upper long side being the front face of the workpiece 90 and its straight left-hand end face being the workpiece edge 92." Leave the remainder of the brief unchanged.

findings.title: FIG. 2 shows the entire rail including its second end but omits the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 required by the description and claims
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (and figures/FIG-1.md), compared with draft/08-detailed-description.md and claims 4, 5, 13 and 18
findings.detail: The FIG. 2 brief specifies a top plan view in which the whole rail lies inside the drawing area from left to right, so both ends of the rail are depicted. The description states that the rail has a transverse center index 24 at its midpoint and a shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 formed in its second end, and claims 4, 5, 13 and 18 require both features. Because the FIG. 2 brief never mentions either feature, the plan view would show the second end of the same rail unnotched and the midpoint unmarked, so the rail as depicted in FIG. 2 would be inconsistent with the rail depicted in FIG. 7 and with the description and claims. FIG. 1 has the same silent omission for the second end of the rail.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "The long, straight rail 10 is seen from above and extends across the drawing area from left to right, well clear of the drawing area borders," with a numeral list containing only 10, 16, 18, 30, 50, 62, 70, 82. Description: "the rail 10 has a transverse center index 24 at its midpoint" and "A shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 (FIG. 7) is formed in the second end of the rail 10 and is aligned with the transverse center index 24." Disclosure: "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint. A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index."
findings.fix: Add to figures/FIG-2.md, after the distance-marks paragraph: "A transverse center index 24 is a short straight mark on the upper surface of the rail 10 at the midpoint of the rail 10, running across the rail 10 transverse to its length. A shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 is formed in the right-hand second end of the rail 10 and is aligned with the transverse center index 24, shown schematically." Add "- 24: transverse center index" and "- 26: sight notch" to the FIG. 2 numeral list, and add the same shallow V-shaped notch, without a numeral, to the second end of the rail 10 in figures/FIG-1.md so that the same rail is depicted consistently in all views.
